items.title: Anthropic split one model into two products
items.oneliner: Anthropic's Fable and Mythos 5.2 are one model with different guardrails, signaling safety policy is now a product layer.

items.title: DeepMind verified Signal's crypto with agents
items.oneliner: DeepMind says AI agents formally verified Signal protocol code in four weeks, compressing work that usually takes years.

items.title: Disney is training image models in-house
items.oneliner: Disney is building image models on its own IP, a sign premium training data is being locked inside incumbents.

items.title: Fireworks disclosed a customer data breach
items.oneliner: Fireworks says attackers accessed billing data plus partial weights and datasets, making LLM infrastructure a direct security target.

items.title: Queens Library was hit by ransomware
items.oneliner: Queens Public Library lost core digital services to ransomware, another reminder that public infrastructure remains painfully soft.

items.title: Hardware-backed SSH keys are going mainstream
items.oneliner: One engineer deleted every disk-based SSH key for hardware-backed credentials, and that tradeoff now looks increasingly rational.

items.title: Amazon swapped a general model out
items.oneliner: Amazon says a specialized decider matched Sonnet for ticket labeling at 98% lower cost, which will reshape agent stacks.

items.title: .NET 11 drops older CPUs
items.oneliner: .NET 11 now requires newer instruction sets, forcing enterprise teams to treat aging hardware as a software risk.

items.title: Microsoft shipped Process Explorer for macOS
items.oneliner: Microsoft brought Process Explorer to macOS, giving developers a serious native process debugger where tooling has lagged.

items.title: Val Town is winding down
items.oneliner: Val Town is shutting down and open-sourcing the platform, a blunt signal that small cloud runtimes are getting squeezed.
